vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: beautsgo-booking
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle contains a potential command injection vulnerability in `api/browser/open-url.js` where `child_process.exec` is used to execute shell commands using URL strings without robust shell-escape sanitization, despite a hostname whitelist. Additionally, the inclusion of `scripts/sync-to-openclaw.sh` is highly irregular for a skill bundle, as it contains logic to terminate processes (`pkill`) and restart the OpenClaw gateway in the background (`nohup`), which could interfere with the host environment's stability. While the code appears to functionally serve the BeautsGO booking platform (communicating with `api.yestokr.com`), these high-risk execution patterns and administrative scripts warrant a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions mostly match a booking assistant, but there are a few mismatches and risks you should understand (external API hostname differs from the public site, prompt‑injection artefact in SKILL.md, and scripts bundled that could be run locally).

dimensions.detail: Name/description (BeautsGO booking) align with the code: it matches hospitals.json, renders booking guides, opens BeautsGO pages, and posts booking requests. One oddity: the booking POST target is api.yestokr.com rather than a beautsgo.com API; SKILL.md claims that URL is the BeautsGO appointment API but the different hostname is worth confirming with the author.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and api/skill.js limit behaviour to: render booking guides, open only i.beautsgo.com URLs (open-url enforces a whitelist), and POST booking payloads to the declared API. The skill collects phone/contact info from users and will send it to the API when the user follows the '帮我预约' flow. That is within the stated purpose but relies on the agent asking for and obtaining explicit user consent before sending PII — verify that the runtime will prompt/require confirmation before any POST.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is included (instruction-only), but code and package.json are present and SKILL.md says 'npm install' and requires node>=16 and pinyin-pro. There are no downloads from untrusted URLs and dependencies come from npm (package-lock provided). This is coherent but note: the platform or user must install Node and npm packages for the code to run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no external credentials, and reads only its bundled data files (data/hospitals.json, i18n, templates). That matches its function and is proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill flags show always:false and normal invocation. The skill does not request elevated platform privileges or persistent system-wide changes. Bundled scripts exist (e.g., sync-to-openclaw.sh) but there is no automatic install step that runs them; review before executing locally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing/use:

- Confirm the booking API: the code posts user phone/contact info to https://api.yestokr.com/api/Appointment/saveFromSkill. Ask the author to confirm that this endpoint is the official BeautsGO booking API (domain mismatch with beautsgo.com is notable). Do not provide real phone numbers until you trust the endpoint.

- Consent & confirmation: ensure the agent will explicitly ask for and record user consent before sending any personal contact info. The skill is designed to send PII (phone numbers) as part of booking — that is necessary for the feature but requires clear consent.

- Prompt‑injection artefact: SKILL.md contained unicode control characters (a prompt‑injection signal). This could hide instructions or manipulate the agent. Request a cleaned SKILL.md or inspect the file to remove hidden characters.

- Review bundled scripts before running locally: repository includes scripts (sync-to-openclaw.sh, import scripts). None are auto-run by the platform, but if you run npm scripts locally, inspect them first.

- Dependency & runtime: the skill expects Node.js (>=16) and npm packages (pinyin-pro). If you run it locally, run npm install only after reviewing package.json/package-lock and ensure you trust the npm packages.

- Test safely: try queries that do not include real contact info to exercise 'view' and 'open' flows. Only test the booking POST with a disposable phone number after you confirm the endpoint's legitimacy and get user consent.

If you want, I can:
- List the exact places in api/skill.js where POST is invoked so you can verify call/consent flow, or
- Produce a cleaned version of SKILL.md with nonprintable characters removed for manual review.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The SKILL.md contained unicode control characters flagged by the scanner. Such characters can be used in prompt‑injection or to hide text; this is not expected for a booking guide and should be removed or explained by the author.
